cards.title: What a conditional is
points: One half sets a condition, the other says what follows.
The tenses are the signal: fact · real future · unreal now.
A comma only appears if the **if**-half comes first.

cards.title: Three types you already have
points: Zero and first came earlier. This one is the second.
Keep the three jobs apart — the form follows the job.

cards.title: Zero and first, side by side

rows: If you heat ice, it melts.
~~If you will heat ice, it melts.~~
If I am tired, I go to bed early.
If it rains tomorrow, I **will** stay home.

points: Zero: both halves in the present. First: present in the if-half, **will** in the result.
Czech marks the future in both halves. English marks it in one.

cards.title: Second conditional
points: **would** + plain verb — travel, not travels and not to travel.
Past in the if-half is distance from reality, not a story about yesterday.

cards.title: Same idea, three stances

table.caption: rain · stay home
rows: If it rains, I stay home.
If it rains tomorrow, I **will** stay home.
If it rained tomorrow, I **would** stay home.

points: First if-half: rains. Second if-half: rained.

cards.title: were for every person

rows: If I **were** free on Friday, we could meet.
If she **weren't** busy, she would join us.
If I were you, I would call him today.

points: **was** is heard in speech and is accepted here — **were** is the form to learn.
If I **were** you is the standard way to give advice in English.

cards.title: Questions

rows: Would you move if they offered you the job?
What would you do if you lost your phone?
Would you mind if I opened the window?

points: **would** moves to the front; the if-half keeps its past form.
Nothing else changes — no do, no did.

cards.title: Common mistakes

rows: ~~If I would have more time, I would travel more.~~
If I **had** more time, I would travel more.
~~If I have more time, I would travel more.~~
If I **had** more time, I would travel more.
~~If I had more time, I will travel more.~~
If I had more time, I **would** travel more.
~~If she lived in Brno, we would to meet.~~
If she lived in Brno, we **would meet** more often.

points: Czech puts *by* in both halves, so **would** wants to jump into the if-half. It cannot.
After **would** comes the plain verb — no to, no -s, no past.
